title: A natural stance and clearer Bar play
changes: Automatic framing uses a lower, closer playing view and tighter bounds around the visible balls. Cue alignment remains adjustable and never overrides a shot being pulled.
Automatic camera framing now swings behind the cue toward the majority of the current player’s legal targets, including the final 8-Ball, with the idle cue facing forward from the new view.

Bar house rules now keep the layout after an empty break instead of automatically reracking. Players alternate until a legal pot assigns groups; pots made with a scratch stay down without assigning a group.
Turn, foul, and result messages use the AI opponent’s name consistently. Illegal-break reracks now explain the missing pocket and four-rail requirement.
Once groups are assigned, player cards show the 8-Ball after their group, highlighted when it becomes the final target.
Desktop tables open from behind the cue, looking toward the fresh rack.
Pocketed balls visibly fall into deeper pocket wells before entering the return, while scoring updates immediately.
Release history now includes earlier versions reconstructed from repository history.

title: A better view of the table
changes: New camera controls: enter Move camera mode to orbit with one finger and pinch or pan with two. Focus balls, Whole table, and zoom buttons make adjusting the view easier.
Optional automatic framing follows the remaining balls after a shot settles. Enabled by default on mobile, disabled on desktop; manual camera movement takes priority.
Click the version badge to read this release history.
Warmer lighting, shadows, detailed felt and wood, improved cushions and pockets, table legs, and a visible ball return.
Improved cue geometry and assisted elevation, collision handling, and rolling behavior. Optional fast-forward for fine movements.
Clearer player cards and adaptive instructions, immediate pocket indicators, configurable rail sights and cue ball markings, and a spin reset button.
Bar 8-Ball placement guidance and persistent tutorial dismissal. Browser tests run separately from required deployment checks.

title: Playable 8-Ball, online rooms, and an AI opponent
changes: Added a playable 3D pool table with racked balls, aiming, shot power, spin, cue ball placement, and 8-Ball rules for turns, fouls, and winning.
Added online rooms with join codes and synchronized shots, plus an optional AI opponent. Fixed the AI getting stuck before taking its turn.
Added player scorecards, a compact lobby, felt and wood color settings, and desktop camera orbit with right-drag.
Refined pull-back shot controls, softened the power curve for gentler shots, previewed legal cue ball placement, and made aiming independent of frame rate.
Improved pocket capture and jaw geometry, cushion rebounds, spin and collision behavior, and visible ball rolling. Break shots can use more power than regular shots.
Added game sound effects and an installable web app with offline asset caching.

title: Correct version display in deployed builds
changes: Fixed the version badge by including the version information in deployed builds and correcting where the server reads it.

title: Initial application foundation
changes: Established the browser canvas and backend foundation for the pool simulator; playable pool arrived in a later release.
Added the site version badge and the initial deployment setup.
